clue.text: Keen to get under catch, very anxious

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece getting under another means it is written below it in the column

parts.note: to nail a culprit is to catch them
a keen or biting wind is sharp and cold

explanation.surface: Someone eager to make a catch is in a state of high tension.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the piece meaning keen sits under the piece meaning catch, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: Nail-biting is the idiom for something causing great tension or worry, from the nervous habit.

clue.text: Ice ball with hardened coating

indicators.note: a coating wraps around what it covers, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: jelly or concrete that has hardened has set
an orb is a sphere or ball

explanation.surface: A ball of ice cream given a hard outer shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' reads as frozen water, but it is the dessert sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert of fruit juice and sugar.

clue.text: Uncertain guarantee protects European Community

indicators.note: something that protects surrounds and shields what it guards, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to insure is to guarantee against loss
the standard abbreviation of European Community

explanation.surface: A shaky assurance that the European Community will be shielded.
explanation.definitionFit: Insecure means not firm or sure, so it can stand for uncertain, as in an uncertain footing.

clue.text: Prison officers, staff on board ship

indicators.note: being on board a vessel means being inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a crew is the staff of a ship or team

explanation.surface: Jail guards and other personnel serving aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screws' is British slang for prison warders.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a screw is a prison guard, so screws are prison officers.

clue.text: Morning sickness good in George III's house

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: George III belonged to the royal House of Hanover
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A queasy pregnant royal at the palace of King George III.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning sickness' pretends to mean pregnancy nausea; Hanover was the German royal house of the Georgian kings.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the nausea and headache felt the morning after drinking too much, a jocular morning sickness.

clue.text: Divers coming up, one's a seabird

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: auks are diving seabirds such as guillemots and puffins

explanation.surface: Diving birds surfacing, one of which is a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' suggests people underwater; here it means diving birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a large predatory gull-like seabird that robs other birds of food.

clue.text: Bully taking battle-axe around head of opponent

indicators.note: one piece going around another encloses it

parts.note: a battle-axe or dragon is a fierce, domineering woman

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so just that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of opponent

explanation.surface: An aggressive person grabbing a weapon to swing at an enemy's head.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside DRAGON: DRAG-O-ON. 'Battle-axe' looks like a weapon but is slang for a formidable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce or bully them into doing something, as with soldiers.

clue.text: As is a less stimulating cup defeat, faced in a bad way

definitions.text: As is a less stimulating cup
definitions.note: describes the answer: a less stimulating cup is decaffeinated

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A team crushed in a cup tie and left in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup defeat' reads as a football knockout, but the cup is coffee and only 'defeat, faced in' is mixed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee or tea with the caffeine removed is decaffeinated, so a cup of it gives less of a stimulant kick.

clue.text: Joke finished, laugh

parts.note: a crack is a witty remark or joke
when time is up it is finished

explanation.surface: The comedian ends a gag and gets a chuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack up is the informal phrasal verb for bursting into laughter.

clue.text: Name for a bicycle coined?

parts.note: surface reading: what was the word invented for a bicycle?
setter's reading: a name made of coins, two old British coins put together naming a bicycle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Coined' seems to mean invented, but it means made from coins: the old penny and the farthing, a quarter-penny coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian high-wheeled bicycle was nicknamed after two coins, its big front wheel and small rear wheel resembling them.

clue.text: Stir cereal as putting in black vegetable

indicators.note: putting something in places it inside the other letters
stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be mixed
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: mix the cereal, adding a dark vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix CEREAL AS and slip B in after the fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabrese is a green sprouting broccoli, a vegetable named after Calabria in Italy.

clue.text: Seed: relative burying one

indicators.note: burying something hides it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, a relative
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Granny planting a seed in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a small hard seed, especially of a cereal such as wheat.

clue.text: Force isn't weak

parts.note: F is the symbol for force in physics
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A paradox: strength is not feebleness.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint can mean feeble or lacking strength, as in a faint voice or faint effort.

clue.text: Revolting sweet, it's suggested?

definitions.meaning: second reading: what is sweet is not savoury, which the word playfully implies

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: split as UN-SAVOURY, the word seems to say the food is sweet rather than savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsavoury means disagreeable or morally offensive, while sweet foods are by definition not savoury ones.

clue.text: Still unsure where to look for helicopter, for example?

definitions.text: where to look for helicopter, for example
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a literal location, aloft in the sky

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the second part is taken literally: an aircraft is overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for undecided plans literally describes something airborne, like a helicopter hovering.

clue.text: Typical example ending in Bible, good book

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Bible
pi, short for pious, means good in crosswords
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: The Bible ends, then comes a good book: a model of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect instance or embodiment that sums up a type, a typical example.

clue.text: Tooth end repaired exactly when agreed

indicators.note: something repaired has been reworked and put back together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dentist fixed the broken tip of a tooth at the scheduled appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot is an idiom for punctually, at precisely the arranged time, the dot being the clock mark.

clue.text: Gosh, it was meant to be: a Mediterranean island!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise
sic, printed after a quotation, means it was written thus intentionally
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a destined holiday on a sunny island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was meant to be' sounds like fate, but describes sic, the editorial note that an odd wording is deliberate.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is the French island in the Mediterranean, birthplace of Napoleon.

clue.text: Reproduction of steel car, most distinct

indicators.note: a reproduction is a remade copy, so the letters are made over in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A replica of a classic steel vehicle that is the sharpest of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearest is the superlative of clear, meaning most plainly visible or distinct.

clue.text: Awful experience with dark horse

parts.note: dark as a noun is nightfall, as in after dark
a mare is a female horse

explanation.surface: A bad experience involving a dark horse, the racing outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark horse' reads as one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any terrible ordeal.

clue.text: Respond to all points covered by extreme characters in anger

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is wrapped inside it
the extreme characters of a word are its two outermost letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of anger
the four points of the compass: north, south, west, east

explanation.surface: Replying furiously to every point raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass points sit between A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer a letter or a question is to respond to it; both verbs take an object.

clue.text: Choral piece starts from music of the Eighties, tragically

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A choral piece that borrows from tragic Eighties pop.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short polyphonic choral composition, usually on a sacred text.

clue.text: Time difficult to perceive then?

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one question about time; the two meanings share a spelling but differ in pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a unit of sixty seconds and an adjective for something extremely small.

clue.text: Old Scottish landowner putting one article inside another

indicators.note: a piece placed inside another is enclosed by it

parts.note: the is the definite article, the other article
an is an indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about nesting articles, oddly tied to a Scottish laird.
explanation.walkthrough: English has two articles, a/an and the, so 'one article' and 'another' name both of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A thane was a Scottish clan chief or landholder of rank, as with Macbeth, Thane of Cawdor.

clue.text: Area in church, part perhaps extended

indicators.note: part of a phrase means only a run of its letters is taken

parts.note: found across the two words: letters 5-8 of 'perhaps extended'

explanation.surface: A section of a church that may have been enlarged.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Plain English required in deciphering of integers

indicators.note: something required in another is needed inside it, so it is inserted
deciphering a code rearranges scrambled symbols, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Plain English is needed to decode a set of whole numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain English' reads as one phrase, but plain is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast grassland plain in Tanzania, famous for its wildlife migration.

clue.text: Bunk or beds I strip

indicators.note: bunk is nonsense, so these letters make nonsense until rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting undressed before climbing into bunk or bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' seems a kind of bed beside 'beds', but it signals nonsense, a mix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrobe is to take off one's clothes, to strip.

clue.text: Crossword writer's job disappearing over the horizon!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: composing a puzzle, the work of a setter
second meaning: going down, as the sun does at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: A crossword compiler is called a setter, so the activity shares a name with the sun going down.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting is both composing a crossword and the sun or moon sinking below the horizon.
